unresolved_added: NFLIS drug-identification reports are enforcement/laboratory observations, not direct prevalence, addiction, use, or person counts.
The paper moves between opioids, synthetic opioids, heroin, all drugs, drug incidents, and addicted people without a stable outcome dictionary.
Sparse county-drug cells motivate aggregation, but the missingness pattern, detection limit, and reporting process are not audited.
Replacing 462 counties with 100 zones creates a modifiable areal unit problem and can reverse associations or apparent origins.
The claim that k=100 is the “best case” follows repeated trials but no objective, elbow curve, stability score, or held-out criterion.
Basic K-means does not generally produce equal-radius clusters, contrary to the prose claim.
The stated 2-8 counties per zone is not reconciled with geography, population, land area, or reporting volume.
Coordinate source, geographic precision, and the meter/kilometer semantics of thresholds are not fully frozen in the prose.
Treating missing ACS values as an average can erase vulnerable counties and understate uncertainty.
Appendix K-means code breaks immediately after the first `renew_cluster`, so the published implementation does not iterate to convergence.
Appendix K-means initialization uses the first k cities rather than randomized or robust starts, creating order dependence.
No seed, replicate, inertia comparison, or cluster-stability analysis supports the zone partition.
Summed zone reports are not population-normalized, so large zones can dominate similarity, graph direction, and crisis labels.
A movie recommender is explanatory analogy, not evidence that drug diffusion follows collaborative-filtering assumptions.
Trend correlation, distance, and report size enter similarity without a fully specified common scale or weight calibration.
Pairwise trend correlation is unstable for short, sparse, constant, or zero series; the handling of undefined correlations is incomplete.
Negative correlations and similarity direction are not clearly treated in the top-ten peer selection.
The time-decay value theta=0.7 is asserted and later admitted to be an unsolved parameter.
The time-decay formula’s exponent and indexing are visually/typographically ambiguous and require executable specification.
The 200 km radius is justified by life experience and unspecified tests, not a frozen selection curve or transport mechanism.
Choosing exactly ten similar zones is unvalidated and interacts with the 200 km neighborhood size.
Total report size in the similarity score confounds drug behavior with population, enforcement, and laboratory capacity.
Geographic proximity is not measured travel, prescription, trafficking, or interpersonal flow.
Orienting every edge from higher report count to lower report count assumes diffusion direction rather than estimating it.
High outgoing degree can be produced mechanically by high counts and dense neighbors, so it is not independent source evidence.
The prose screens five candidates and simulates each, while appendix code randomly selects one of the top four degree nodes in a key execution path.
Random-walk seed, stopping rule, path length, revisit handling, and uncertainty across the 100 trials are not reported.
The origin score formula has unclear subscripts, multiplication order, visit-count semantics, and self-node exclusion.
Origin locations are not validated against known historical introductions or a synthetic source-recovery experiment.
Coast/Great Lakes proximity and Ohio/Virginia concentrations are converted to import and legal-enforcement stories without corresponding data.
The paper says an outlier may be a fault or a substantive highlight but never separates measurement error from crisis status.
High raw report counts are read partly as dense population, yet the SVM inputs are not population-normalized.
One-class SVM kernel, nu, gamma, scaling, and sensitivity are incomplete despite their control over the outlier fraction.
One-class SVM pseudo-labels are treated as crisis labels without external health, overdose, prescription, or treatment ground truth.
Training a linear SVM on those pseudo-labels does not provide independent validation of the crisis boundary.
Opioid and total-drug axes need explicit units, transformations, and comparable population denominators.
Appendix threshold code contains a hand-written boundary `TotalDrug < 125000 - 100*Opioid`, which is not reconciled with the trained-model prose.
The paper switches between county-level SVM language and zone-level predictor outputs without a complete mapping contract.
Own-zone and peer-zone SVR features can share spatial and temporal information, so leakage and effective sample size need auditing.
The inverse-error weight formula is typographically corrupted in prose and differs slightly across appendix functions.
The authors say they tried many weight formats and chose the one with almost the smallest test-set error, compromising the claimed 2017 test set.
The later retraining split is described inconsistently with the earlier training/held-out/test split and needs a frozen lineage.
“There is no overfitting” is an absolute unsupported claim, especially after manual feature, weight, kernel, and degree selection.
The SVR grid covers few kernels, degrees, gamma values, and C values; it is not a general method comparison.
The statement that C has almost no influence is not accompanied by the corresponding table, range, or stability analysis.
Predictor scaling and response scaling for SVR are not documented, although kernels and distances depend on them.
Least-square error is reported without units, sample weighting, naive/no-change baselines, or uncertainty.
Negative SVR outputs are truncated to zero in code, but the bias and frequency of truncation are not reported.
Forecast maps and county lists have no prediction intervals, stochastic bands, or threshold uncertainty.
Limiting the forecast to 2018-2019 is responsible, but the two-year claims remain conditional on a seven-year training history.
Crisis-risk maps inherit unvalidated pseudo-labels and a poorly calibrated boundary.
Statements that some areas may increase by thousands omit denominator, baseline, area, drug class, and uncertainty.
Forecast declines are interpreted substantively without distinguishing model shrinkage, peer borrowing, and true improvement.
The mismatch between predicted crisis counties and inferred origin zones is observed but not quantitatively diagnosed.
Denser-population explanations are asserted from maps without population-normalized comparisons.
Historical variation maps provide a visual comparator but no numerical out-of-sample score.
The year and sample used for ACS Booleanization are inconsistent between prose and appendix code.
Two-cluster Booleanization needs label orientation, seed, cluster centers, and year-to-year stability.
Percentage-form ACS variables reduce but do not eliminate population, sampling-error, denominator, and survey-design effects.
Apriori thresholds differ across prose/code paths (including support 0.05/0.06 and confidence 0.75/0.8), so results are not uniquely reproducible.
Support, confidence, and lift describe co-occurrence, not direction, individual risk, or causality.
Running Apriori separately in 16 categories excludes cross-category combinations by construction.
Factor-code-to-human-label provenance and ACS vintage definitions must be versioned.
Ranking antecedents by frequency across rules ignores dependence, multiple testing, and rule redundancy.
“Autocorrelation” in the factor-sign step is vague and is not a formal spatial or temporal diagnostic.
The |corr|>0.8 threshold is arbitrary and no confidence interval or null distribution is supplied.
Appendix correlation code normalizes short time series and then applies a simple correlation without robust missingness or constant-series handling.
Calling three features “still too large” is not justified by the regression sample size or model capacity.
PCA/SVD lacks scaling choice, loadings, explained variance, sign, component stability, and interpretation.
Selected factors are converted into education, age, and female-householder mechanisms that the association pipeline did not identify.
Group labels can stigmatize elder people, women without husbands, and educational groups unless uncertainty and structural context are explicit.
Observational associations and PCA inputs cannot supply effect sizes for scholarships, nursing homes, welfare, pharmaceutical design, or outreach.
Stricter laws and transport checks are recommended from map patterns without enforcement efficacy, civil burden, or displacement analysis.
Replacing an unobservable reduction in within-group addiction probability with a reduction in group population share is not causally equivalent.
The beta parameters for within-group addiction are explicitly unavailable, so the equivalent alpha edits cannot be identified from current data.
Treating a 20% factor reduction as “very successful” is an unsupported policy threshold.
The S approximately equals S-prime assumption is only a local algebraic convenience and fails as demographic edits grow.
Strategy tables use one zone, ambiguous “Total Decrease Rate/Total Drug Reports” headings, no uncertainty, and no realized policy comparator.
The weakness section names radius, decay, and high-dimensional limits but does not propagate them into origin, forecast, or policy uncertainty.

Duplicate Summary text, Contents, References, figure/table cells, formulas, map labels, memo-repeated visuals, and appendix code must not inflate positive human-language counts; appendix/prose divergences must remain explicit warnings.
